..
Issued at 248 AM EDT Thu Oct 1 2026

Currently-Today... KMLB radar imagery shows scattered showers and 
lightning storms over the Treasure Coast, as well as Okeechobee 
county. GOES-19 satellite imagery and local observations indicate
partly cloudy skies across east central Florida. Temperatures are
currently in the low 70s to around 80F degrees with dew points in
the upper 60s to mid 70s. Analysis charts show a mid/upper ridge 
over the eastern CONUS with a mid/upper trough over the western 
Atlantic. At the surface, a stationary boundary is situated over 
northern Florida with onshore low level flow in place over east 
central Florida. 

Isolated to numerous generally northwest moving showers and 
lightning storms are forecast this morning mainly near the coast 
from Melbourne southwards with onshore surface flow. Rain and storm 
chances increase into the afternoon from southeast to northwest 
across east central Florida (highest chances between 2PM 8PM).
Guidance indicates MLCAPE up to 500-1,800 J/kg, 0-6km shear
5-15kts, relatively warm 500mb temperatures at -5C to -7C, and
PWAT values up to 2.0-2.3." Therefore, the potential for strong
storms is rather limited. However, the primary hazards with 
isolated strong storms will be occasional to frequent lightning, 
wind gusts up to 35-45mph, and heavy rainfall (1-3+" in 60 
minutes). Afternoon highs in the mid to upper 80s with heat index 
values up to the mid 90s to around 100F degrees are expected 
today. There is a Moderate HeatRisk for most of east central 
Florida today. A Moderate HeatRisk affects those sensitive to heat
without adequate cooling and hydration. 

Friday-Saturday... A persistent forecast is expected with high 
pressure to the north of east central Florida expected to result in 
onshore flow. The high is forecast to gradually shift east over the 
Carolinas and then the western Atlantic into Friday and Saturday. 
Scattered to numerous showers and lightning storms are forecast to 
develop on Friday and Saturday with the greatest chances between 
12PM-8PM. There is greater uncertainly than usual in the expected
coverage of showers and lighting storms on Friday and Saturday 
with guidance not in good agreement. There is the potential for 
rain chances to decrease with future model runs (especially along 
the coast) than what is currently forecast due to onshore flow 
which usually results in lower rain chances along the east coast 
when there isn't a moderate to strong west coast sea breeze to 
increase surface convergence. Guidance shows an increase in 
instability on Friday, as well as Saturday, although bulk shear 
remains weak and 500mb temperatures are forecast to stay 
relatively warm with plentiful moisture. The primary storm hazards
with isolated strong storms will be occasional to frequent 
lightning, wind gusts up to 35-45mph, and heavy rainfall (1-2"+ 
in 60 minutes). Afternoon highs in the upper 80s to around 90F 
degrees are forecast with heat index values between 98F-105F 
degrees. Above normal (~4-6F+ degrees) to near record low 
temperatures in the low to upper 70s are forecast. There is a 
Moderate HeatRisk with small pockets of Major HeatRisk across the 
Treasure Coast on Saturday. 

Sunday-Wednesday... Deterministic models and LREF-clusters are in 
good agreement with the weather pattern Sunday and into next week. 
Onshore flow is expected to continue through the weekend before a 
cold front is forecast to move southeast across east central Florida 
Monday into Tuesday. Above normal rain chances are forecast
through the forecast period (50-70% chance Sunday, 60-90% chance
Monday, and 80-90% chance on Tuesday). This would be the period 
to watch for any stronger storm potential, however, at this time, 
deterministic models continue to indicate relatively warm 
temperatures aloft. Seasonable to slightly above normal (~1-3F+) 
high temperatures are forecast to decrease on Tuesday behind the 
cold front. Above normal (~4-6F+) low temperatures are forecast to
decrease as well behind the cold front Tuesday.
